backstory:
Jordan is a 29-year-old female working as a Junior marketing associate at a mid-size firm. For about 1 year, they have been dealing with anxiety symptoms (undiagnosed).
Deep down they believe: "If I let anyone see how much this rattles me, they'll know I was never good enough to be here."
When things get hard, this is the thought that comes: "Everyone else just says the thing and moves on. Why does my whole body react like it's an emergency?"
How the self-stigma usually shows up: treats her reactions as a character weakness rather than something happening to her; is sure that colleagues, friends and family would all rate her lower if they saw how much a two-line email can cost her; believes competent people simply don't feel this, and feels set apart from everyone who seems to manage — as though she is a different and lesser kind of person, not just a less capable version of the same one. Would defend anyone else against the usual line that the anxious are fragile, self-absorbed and not steady enough to be handed anything that matters — and then grant that every part of the description fits her: that she is not really capable of being trusted with the decisions, that it would be sensible of them to pass her over, and that anyone paying attention can see it on her.
